moodboard.title: Wim Bakery: halftone 'flour' photography with lime type over it
reasons: the work itself was viewed (visual analysis)
moodboard.principle: Convert product photos into a coarse grain or stipple texture so that big bold type can sit directly on top without the image fighting it.

seen.whatWasSeen: Large project photos of the identity: the lime-grid logo hero, a menu board, cups and containers, a sidewalk A-board, a T-shirt graphic, a tote, and a grainy pastry pattern with lime type. This is an identity system shown in use, not an ad campaign.
seen.composition: The hero is a square lime field with a thin white square grid (like bench tiles). A heavy black blobby croissant-like symbol sits above a two-line stacked 'WIM / Bakery' wordmark, all centred. Applications either put this grid on lids and cups, or place grainy stipple photos of pastries scattered loosely across a white or black field with type over them.
seen.typography: A neutral, heavy grotesque sans used throughout (bold for the wordmark, regular for menu lists). It is set tight, with large type in two stacked lines, flush left on signage and centred on the logo. The organic croissant-like mark contrasts with the plain type.

corrections.wasClaimed: the wordmark is shaped to fit the curve of a croissant
corrections.actuallySeen: The 'WIM Bakery' lettering itself looks like a regular heavy grotesque. The croissant reference is the separate organic blob symbol above it. I could not confirm that the letterforms are shaped to a curve.

corrections.wasClaimed: lime 'WIM Bakery' type on top of the grainy image
corrections.actuallySeen: True for the pattern piece and the T-shirt, but the A-board and menu use black type over a pale lime or grainy background, so lime type over the image is one variant, not the rule.

moodboard.title: With Wheat: fine-outline bread illustrations 'filled' with bright colour
reasons: the work itself was viewed (visual analysis)
moodboard.principle: Draw each product as one flat silhouette in a limited warm palette and print it at near life size on its own pack, so the packaging shows what is inside.

seen.whatWasSeen: A hero photo of two white carrier bags plus a cup with real baguettes, and two large flat-lay grids of the full packaging range (kraft and white bags, sleeves, cups, boxes, cards), clearly legible.
seen.composition: On the carrier bags, a pile of simplified bread and pastry illustrations fills the lower half of the white bag, with the logo centred in the upper third and lots of empty white above. On the product bags and sleeves, each item gets one large silhouette of the specific bread inside (a long baguette, a round doughnut, a toast slice), filling the bag.
seen.typography: The logo pairs a geometric, custom-drawn Chinese wordmark with a small, widely tracked Latin all-caps line. On kraft bags 'WITH WHEAT' is stacked in a heavy geometric sans, and product names in English and Chinese are set vertically.

corrections.wasClaimed: Illustrations sit on bags so they peek out at the top alongside real baguettes
corrections.actuallySeen: The illustrations sit in the lower half of the bags. It's the real baguettes and pastries that stick out of the top of the bags.

corrections.wasClaimed: MINIMAL_COPY / GENEROUS_NEGATIVE_SPACE as dominant
corrections.actuallySeen: Generous space is true for the white carrier bags only. The kraft product bags are fairly full: a large silhouette, a vertical bilingual name and a stacked wordmark.

moodboard.title: Burger King 'Moldy Whopper': the decaying product as proof
reasons: the work itself was viewed (visual analysis)
moodboard.principle: Shoot the product as a macro texture on black with dramatic side light, and let only a tiny label and a small centred logo frame it, so the image becomes a still life.

seen.whatWasSeen: Four portrait print/poster executions (Day 28, Day 32, Day 33, Day 35, or similar), large enough to read the day labels and tagline. The film was present but not watched.
seen.composition: Each portrait poster is an extreme close crop of the mouldy burger, filling and bleeding off the frame (often the right edge or the top and bottom), set against black. Some show the whole side profile; others zoom so far in that only stacked layers of bun, patty and lettuce are visible as horizontal bands.
seen.typography: Labels are tiny: 'The Whopper' in a plain small sans followed by 'DAY 28' (and so on) in a hand-lettered or stencil-like style, like a lab-sample label. The tagline is set in widely letterspaced small capitals in a light sans, all white.

corrections.wasClaimed: The Whopper and its ingredients as the single subject (implying a whole burger)
corrections.actuallySeen: Most executions are extreme macro crops that bleed off the frame. Several show only a few stacked layers, not a whole recognisable burger.

corrections.wasClaimed: Typeface details are not described / short supporting line
corrections.actuallySeen: There's a tiny corner label ('The Whopper' plus a hand-lettered-looking 'DAY 28'), and the tagline is in widely tracked small capitals beneath a small centred logo.

corrections.wasClaimed: Not described beyond natural colours
corrections.actuallySeen: A black background throughout, which makes the teal, white and orange mould stand out.

moodboard.title: Roladin Hanukkah posters: a person holding one doughnut on red
reasons: the work itself was viewed (visual analysis)
moodboard.principle: Style the person's hair, make-up and wardrobe to echo the product's colours and toppings, and use a seamless backdrop in the same family. The match then becomes the message without a headline.

seen.whatWasSeen: Six portrait posters from Roladin's 2017 'Sufganiyot Collection' on Ads of the World, clearly legible, including the woman in a red dress that Poster House catalogues. The Poster House pages (p=17915 'I'm Simple' 2020 and p=17913) loaded but their poster images were broken (0px), so the 2020 'I'm Simple' poster was NOT seen.
seen.composition: A fashion-style half-length portrait, model centred or slightly right, against a seamless coloured studio backdrop. One hand holds a single elaborate doughnut at about chest or shoulder height, in focus in the lower-left quadrant. A small logo lock-up sits in the top-left corner.
seen.typography: Almost none: a tiny, widely tracked all-caps sans line plus the existing Roladin logo (red mark and serif-style caps in a white box). Copy is not part of the idea.

corrections.wasClaimed: Red is prominent; 2017 poster shows a woman in a red dress on red
corrections.actuallySeen: In the 2017 set the backdrops vary per poster (burgundy, mauve, grey, indigo, teal, slate). The red-dress poster is on deep indigo, and red is not a constant.

corrections.wasClaimed: a person holding one doughnut on red
corrections.actuallySeen: Only the 2020 'I'm Simple' poster (not seen; Poster House image broken) is described as on red. The 2017 posters seen are fashion portraits on varied backdrop colours.

corrections.wasClaimed: possibly an 'I'm ___' line per poster
corrections.actuallySeen: The 2017 posters carry no headline at all, only a tiny 'THE SUFGANIYOT COLLECTION' line and the logo. The 2020 'I'm ___' copy remains unverified.

moodboard.title: Carrefour Flasher Flood: the price-offer ad pushed to parody
reasons: brings the craft of a OFFER campaign (cross-industry: ecommerce)
moodboard.principle: Repeat the category's most clichéd element (here a price flasher) thousands of times until it becomes a texture, and put the whole message in one corner badge.

seen.whatWasSeen: The full portrait poster from the D&AD archive, viewed whole and with the top-left corner zoomed. The overall structure and the corner starburst copy are clear; individual products and prices are too tiny to identify.
seen.composition: A portrait poster with a plain white border around an edge-to-edge field of thousands of tiny product cut-outs, each covered by a small red circular price flasher. The density is uniform from corner to corner, so from a distance the whole field reads as one speckled red texture. The only distinct element is a larger red starburst in the top-left corner.
seen.typography: Almost none: inside the corner starburst, 'Low prices storewide' in bold yellow sans over the white Carrefour wordmark and logo. The flashers carry tiny white price numerals that are unreadable at poster scale.

corrections.wasClaimed: the mass of price bursts reads first, then individual prices
corrections.actuallySeen: Correct for the mass, but individual prices are too small to read at all. The second read is the single larger starburst in the top-left corner carrying 'Low prices storewide' and the Carrefour logo.

corrections.wasClaimed: VIBRANT_COMPLEMENTARY, COLLAGE_GRID
corrections.actuallySeen: The palette is essentially one red with small product specks and one yellow badge, not a complementary scheme. The items are packed as an all-over pattern rather than arranged in a grid.

moodboard.title: Coco Reformer Pilates: warm, real-member launch for a neighbourhood studio
reasons: the work itself was viewed (visual analysis)
moodboard.principle: Pair a bright daylight photo of a real instructor with a calm solid colour band holding one short friendly sentence; the band keeps type off the photo and the feed looks consistent.

seen.whatWasSeen: Hero photo with logo, exterior blade/fascia signage, wayfinding signs ('Pause your pings...', 'Shoes off...'), the interlocking COCO mark on brown, a photographed lounge poster (readable only at small size), socks, bottle, bra merch, website/phone mockups, and a carousel of about eight Instagram post mockups. The Instagram posts were large enough to judge layout and type.
seen.composition: Social posts are mostly a full-width natural-light studio photo (instructor or members on reformers) with, on some posts, a solid colour band underneath carrying one short line ('Sundays just got happier!', 'Private classes for small groups: now at Coco!') or a quote card on brown ('Beautiful, airy and spacious.').
seen.typography: The COCO wordmark is a wide, high-contrast flared serif in caps with crescent-like Cs; supporting copy and signage use a clean geometric/humanist sans in sentence case; the lounge poster uses serif headlines. Quote cards set a centred sans in large size with quote marks.

corrections.wasClaimed: Grounding brown with airy lavenders and blues.
corrections.actuallySeen: Confirmed in spirit, but the dominant tones are greige/taupe and a deep mauve-brown; the blue is a pale periwinkle used only for small text bands; lavender is barely visible.

corrections.wasClaimed: MINIMAL_COPY and TYPE_AS_IMAGE across the work.
corrections.actuallySeen: TYPE_AS_IMAGE is only in the identity panels (interlocking COCO pattern), not in the ads; the social ads are photo-plus-caption-band layouts.

corrections.wasClaimed: Not detailed.
corrections.actuallySeen: Social posts: photo first, short line in colour band second, small price/detail third; no logo on the image itself.

moodboard.title: Misfits fitness programme: oversized type that 'takes up space' with athletes in action
reasons: the work itself was viewed (visual analysis)
moodboard.principle: Pair one huge, stretched condensed keyword with small lowercase serif connector words; the size contrast creates hierarchy and warmth together.

seen.whatWasSeen: Hero split image, a 'WORKING OUT, / NOT FITTING IN' square diptych, the 'act like YOU OWN the place' split graphic, a repeating MISFITS banner with cut-out figures, the 'MAKE ROOM' layout, and a nine-tile social grid ('NOT LONG NOW...', 'meet your TRAINERS', 'HEADS UP.', 'room for'). All large enough to read.
seen.composition: Black-and-white cut-out figures (often flipped upside down or mid-jump) placed around very tall condensed words; frequent two-panel splits (type panel + photo panel), and square social tiles with type and a small cut-out athlete.
seen.typography: A very tall, tightly condensed sans in caps, digitally stretched or warped in perspective, paired with a soft, friendly lowercase serif for connecting words. The contrast between huge condensed caps and small soft serif is the signature.

corrections.wasClaimed: 'MAKE ROOM' graphic with stretched pink type and two kettlebell photos.
corrections.actuallySeen: Two black-and-white cut-outs of the same person squatting with a kettlebell, placed diagonally opposite each other, on a light grey field.

corrections.wasClaimed: Oversized, three-dimensional-looking type.
corrections.actuallySeen: Type reads as a very tall condensed sans that is stretched or warped in perspective; the 3D feel comes from the warping, not from extrusion or shading. The soft serif (lowercase) is used for small connector words.

corrections.wasClaimed: Vibrant green and purple added.
corrections.actuallySeen: The 'green' reads as a neon lime-yellow; main fields are lime, pink, violet, black and off-white.

corrections.wasClaimed: Black-and-white and colour photos.
corrections.actuallySeen: Mostly black-and-white cut-outs; colour photography appears in the hero and one social tile portrait.

moodboard.title: Bon Elliot launch: Penn-style still life and 'under the microscope' editorial
reasons: the work itself was viewed (visual analysis)
moodboard.principle: Pair two images across a spread (product close-up beside a human or metaphor image) and link them with one thin line of text at mid-height.

seen.whatWasSeen: The hero two-page spread (backlit profile silhouette holding a bottle / close-up bottle and cap), a collage spread of combs, rings and bottles in red-orange, a twin-bottle spread, a face-plus-hand-holding-bottle spread, a three-panel still-life spread, a 3D logo object, orange packaging on black and on pale blue, a nine-image grid (tomato, skin cells, eyes, bottle, lab diagram) and a stacked-tomatoes / portrait diptych. Large enough to judge layout; the small caption text is not legible.
seen.composition: Magazine-style spreads split down the gutter into two images (diptychs) or three vertical panels; each half has one centred subject (bottle, face, tomato stack) photographed frontally and symmetrically.
seen.typography: The BON ELLIOT wordmark is a stacked, bold geometric sans in caps (Avant Garde style), used tiny in layouts and large only on the bottles; captions are tiny sans in one line; packaging uses widely tracked caps for 'A NEW MODEL FOR SKIN HEALTH'.

corrections.wasClaimed: Bright orange boxes against dark and pale blue backgrounds as the campaign's punch.
corrections.actuallySeen: Confirmed; also the red-orange appears in the photography itself (tomatoes, combs, rings), not only on packaging.

corrections.wasClaimed: CUTOUT_PRODUCT_ON_COLOR.
corrections.actuallySeen: Products are photographed in-scene with real lighting and shadows on pale backgrounds, not cut out onto flat colour.

corrections.wasClaimed: Short headline 'A NEW MODEL FOR SKIN HEALTH'.
corrections.actuallySeen: That line appears on packaging in small tracked caps, not as a large headline on the campaign spreads, which carry only a tiny caption line.

moodboard.title: Equinox 'Commit to Something': lifestyle tableaux with one centred slogan
reasons: the work itself was viewed (visual analysis)
moodboard.principle: Set a short slogan in a thin, widely tracked sans across the image so a provocative photo stays dominant and the type reads as a premium signature.

seen.whatWasSeen: All 7 finished executions as large landscape images on the article page (restaurant/breastfeeding, woodland, trophy room, money on a sofa, night street with red-and-black outfit, bed of entwined bodies, plus the hero), large enough to read the slogan and logo.
seen.composition: Every execution is a full-bleed landscape photograph with the subject centred; the slogan runs as a single horizontal line across the middle, sitting at roughly 50-60% of the height so it crosses the subject's torso rather than the face.
seen.typography: The slogan is set in a thin, wide, monoline sans in all caps with generous letter-spacing, spanning about 80% of the image width; it is white with no shadow or panel. The EQUINOX wordmark is tiny (about 3-4% of height), heavily tracked caps, centred near the bottom edge.

corrections.wasClaimed: One slogan in large white capitals (implied bold, weight not stated).
corrections.actuallySeen: The slogan is a thin/light, wide, generously tracked monoline sans: large in width but very light in weight, closer to a fashion-editorial line than a bold headline.

corrections.wasClaimed: Dim, dramatic, low-key scenes.
corrections.actuallySeen: Not all are dim: the trophy room, sofa and bed scenes are evenly and fairly brightly lit. The consistent element is a cool teal/cyan colour grade, not darkness.

corrections.wasClaimed: Slogan centred, logo at the bottom.
corrections.actuallySeen: Confirmed; additionally all executions shown are landscape, the slogan sits slightly below the vertical centre, and the logo is a tiny tracked wordmark bottom-centre.

moodboard.title: Sweaty Betty 'Don't sweat it': candid laughing people and conversational headlines
reasons: the work itself was viewed (visual analysis)
moodboard.principle: Anchor every piece with the same two corner marks (wordmark top-left, symbol top-right) so the content area can vary freely.

seen.whatWasSeen: Landscape 'Don't sweat it' campaign image, a '25 YEARS STRONG' image, a nine-tile social grid (bra fit, Black Friday, Night Vision, half-marathon distances, Power Pro, Colour Theory, In with the new, athlete quote, chrome 25), a 'Designed to release a rush' landscape, 'Recharge.' and a second 'Don't sweat it' video still, an orange-purple gradient 'Embracing our bodies...' poster, the 'Shaped by our Sisterhood' group shot and a photographed shop window 'New year. Same you.', plus packaging/merch. All large enough to read.
seen.composition: A fixed frame: SWEATY BETTY wordmark small in the top-left corner, the four-dot symbol small in the top-right, and a short headline set large in the lower-left third over a full-bleed photo or a flat/gradient field.
seen.typography: A clean grotesk in sentence case (not all caps), medium-to-semibold weight, tight leading, lines set flush left; headlines run to 3-4 lines on gradient posters ('Embracing our bodies and what we can do with them'). Occasional special treatments: chrome/liquid-metal 3D numerals and letters for the 25th anniversary, and a glowing lime 'Recharge.'.

corrections.wasClaimed: Large headline type (weight/case not specified).
corrections.actuallySeen: Headlines are in sentence case in a medium-weight grotesk, not caps or heavy display; the 25th-anniversary pieces add chrome 3D letterforms.

corrections.wasClaimed: Shop-window poster with a purple border.
corrections.actuallySeen: The window shows a purple-outlined frame containing a photo backdrop with orange headline across mannequins; the border is part of a window graphic, not a printed poster frame.

corrections.wasClaimed: Orange as the anchor.
corrections.actuallySeen: Confirmed, but the system also leans on electric blue, pale lime and burgundy type; the orange reads as coral-red.
